title: Flow, Pressure, Line Loss & Installed Delivery

content.overview: Installed irrigation performance depends on source pressure, regulators, line length, elevation, filters, valves and emitter behavior. A printed emitter rating or controller schedule is a design assumption, not proof of delivered output.

vocabulary.definition: Volume of water delivered per unit time.
Force per unit area available to move water through the irrigation system.
Pressure/energy loss caused by friction, fittings, elevation and flow through the system.

sections.title: Nominal output is not installed output
sections.body: Emitter ratings assume defined test conditions. Installed delivery can differ because of pressure, clogging, regulator performance, filtration and system configuration.

sections.title: Pressure evidence adds context to flow
sections.body: Low far-end flow with low pressure suggests a different fault class from one isolated low emitter under otherwise stable pressure.

sections.title: Controller command does not prove water arrived
sections.body: Use measured delivery and root-zone response to verify actual irrigation rather than relying on schedules or command logs alone.

workedExamples: A zone command completes normally, but catch volumes are low at the far end. The controller log confirms intent, not delivery.
commonMistakes: Using emitter labels as current performance data.
Treating scheduled runtime as delivered volume.
content.practicalApplication: Map a mock zone using source pressure, midline/far-end pressure and emitter catch volumes, then classify the likely fault domain.
content.summary: Irrigation performance must be measured in the installed system, not inferred from labels or schedules.
